protocols.name: Activation patching: denoising (clean→corrupt) and noising (corrupt→clean)
protocols.detail: Run clean and corrupted prompts; overwrite selected activations from one run into the other; measure effect on outputs across components/layers.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

protocols.name: Exploratory→confirmatory granularity sweep
protocols.detail: Start with coarse residual/layer sweeps to locate effects, then refine to heads/MLPs/neurons/features; conclude with path patching and multi-component tests.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

protocols.name: Paired-run patching with baseline, perturbed, and patched passes
protocols.detail: Cache activations on baseline and perturbed inputs; construct patched run on the lower-performing input with targeted activations swapped; record final-score changes.
evidence: MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

protocols.name: Prompt distribution design
protocols.detail: Use narrow variations for sensitive exploratory patches; use a wide distribution varying hypothesized variables for confirmatory tests.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

protocols.name: Intervention-strength (alpha) sweep
protocols.detail: Vary the injection/steering strength across a range (including alpha=0) to establish dose–response and detect non-monotonicity.
evidence: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations
How to use and interpret activation patching
Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations

protocols.name: Report multiple output metrics per patch
protocols.detail: Log and compare several metrics (e.g., logit diff, logprob, KL, accuracy) for each patch; inspect agreement and per-answer logits.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

protocols.name: Length-matched inputs for content perturbations
protocols.detail: Maintain equal token lengths (e.g., via padding) between baseline and perturbed pairs to isolate content effects.
evidence: MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

protocols.name: Layerwise SAE evaluation and injection
protocols.detail: Train SAEs, report %ExplainedVar and L0 per layer, and inject reconstructions/zero-ablations layerwise to measure causal effects on loss.
evidence: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video

protocols.name: Ablation evaluation with zero vs mean ablation
protocols.detail: Assess circuit causal relevance by zero-ablation; compare to mean-ablation to detect ablation-artifacts and size of minimal circuits.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

protocols.name: Attribution stability via repeated runs
protocols.detail: Repeat attribution/patching over multiple batches; retain only consistently discovered edges/components by a predefined consistency threshold.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

protocols.name: Input corruption / synonym splits for shortcut checks
protocols.detail: Replace schema names or use Synonym/Natural variants to test whether behavior relies on surface-name shortcuts.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

protocols.name: Formal verification + adversarial evaluation of IRNs
protocols.detail: Compute certified bounds (δ, Jaccard lower bound) with a verifier and empirical bounds via attacks; report both across layers.
evidence: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

protocols.name: Instrumentation validation for interventions and hooks
protocols.detail: Automated tests to check tensor shapes, attention-prob normalization, non-noop interventions, and causality-preserving layer skips before experiments.
evidence: nnterp: A Standardized Interface for Mechanistic Interpretability of Transformers

controls.name: Zero ablation baseline
controls.detail: Overwrite targeted activations with zeros and measure degradation compared to patched/injected runs.
controls.rules_out: That observed effects require special baselines; shows behavior change is not due to arbitrary removal but to specific content in activations.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

controls.name: Mean ablation baseline
controls.detail: Replace targeted activations with their dataset mean.
controls.rules_out: That effects are artifacts of using zero as the ablation baseline rather than content-specific changes.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

controls.name: Size-matched random subset of intervened components/directions
controls.detail: Use a random set of components/features or a random direction with the same size/norm and intervention strength as the hypothesized mechanism.
controls.rules_out: That improvements or failures arise from generic perturbation or chance rather than targeted, task-relevant structure.
evidence: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

controls.name: Reverse-direction patching (compare denoising vs noising)
controls.detail: Run both clean→corrupt and corrupt→clean patching for the same targets.
controls.rules_out: Direction-specific artifacts in necessity/sufficiency claims about components.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

controls.name: Path patching vs component-output patching
controls.detail: Restrict patches to specific A→B paths and compare to full-output component patches.
controls.rules_out: Mediation vs direct-effect confusion; distinguishes mediated effects from direct interactions.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

controls.name: Baseline/perturbed runs without patching
controls.detail: Run both inputs without activation swaps and cache activations.
controls.rules_out: That patched-run effects simply mirror the direct effect of perturbation or run variance, not the swap itself.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

controls.name: Length-matched padded baseline
controls.detail: Pad baseline inputs to match perturbed input lengths.
controls.rules_out: Token-length/padding differences driving observed effects instead of content changes.
evidence: MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

controls.name: Input corruption / synonym-variant evaluation
controls.detail: Evaluate on Synonym/Natural dataset variants or corrupted inputs.
controls.rules_out: Shortcut reliance on surface forms (e.g., name matching) rather than semantic mechanisms.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

controls.name: Retain-entire-layer when any head flagged
controls.detail: During ablations, keep the whole layer (heads/MLP) if any head is implicated.
controls.rules_out: False negatives from distributed computation or omitted MLP contributions when testing head-only circuits.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

controls.name: Token-type configuration controls (CLS-only vs spatial vs all patches)
controls.detail: Train/evaluate SAEs on different token subsets and compare injection/ablation effects.
controls.rules_out: Token-agnostic explanations for SAE effects; attributes differences to token-type specialization.
evidence: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video

controls.name: Architecture comparison (bi-encoder vs cross-encoder)
controls.detail: Run identical perturbation/patching analyses across architectures.
controls.rules_out: Backbone-agnostic explanations; identifies architecture-dependent phenomena.
evidence: MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval

controls.name: Gaussian-noise corruption source
controls.detail: Use noise-added corrupt prompts as the source in clean→corrupt patching.
controls.rules_out: Dependence on idiosyncratic corrupted prompts; tests robustness of patching conclusions.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

controls.name: Intervention-strength (alpha) sweep including alpha=0
controls.detail: Evaluate multiple strengths (including none) for the same intervention vector.
controls.rules_out: Artifacts of a single, arbitrary intervention magnitude; establishes dose–response.
evidence: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations

confounds.name: Ablation-method artifact (mean vs zero)
confounds.detail: Compact circuits from mean-ablation may not causally reproduce behavior, mimicking positive results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare zero- and mean-ablation against size-matched random circuits; treat mean-ablation circuits cautiously when performance aligns with random.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

confounds.name: Redundancy/compensation masks causal roles
confounds.detail: Backup components or residual-stream compensation can hide necessity when intervening on a single layer/component.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Patch or ablate multiple hypothesized components jointly; use path patching and multi-layer interventions to reveal masked effects.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations

confounds.name: Metric-driven false positives (damaging competitors)
confounds.detail: Improved logit difference can come from suppressing incorrect answers rather than restoring the correct signal.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Inspect individual logits/logprobs and report KL divergence/multiple metrics to detect indiscriminate degradation.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

confounds.name: Prompt/distribution specificity
confounds.detail: Effects found on a narrow corruption set may not generalize.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Replicate across multiple corrupted prompt distributions and confirm on a wide distribution varying circuit variables.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

confounds.name: Mediation vs amplification/confounding pathways
confounds.detail: Component effects may be indirect via other mediators rather than direct interactions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use path patching to isolate A→B→C vs A→C paths and test necessity/sufficiency per path.
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching

confounds.name: Shortcut reliance on surface names/strings
confounds.detail: Apparent text-to-SQL competence may stem from verbatim name matching.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Input corruption and Synonym/Natural dataset variants that require semantic mapping; observe performance changes.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

confounds.name: Distributed computation/MLP involvement hides true circuit
confounds.detail: Head-only identification may miss layer-level or MLP contributions, yielding false negatives.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Retain entire implicated layers and include MLPs in mappings; compare recovered accuracy with/without MLPs.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

confounds.name: Poor identifiability of SAE features
confounds.detail: Sparse features may not correspond to causal components, making overlaps incidental.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Quantify SAE–EAP circuit overlap vs random and evaluate recovered accuracy from SAE-selected circuits.
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research

confounds.name: General perturbation, not targeted causal change
confounds.detail: Observed corrections could be due to arbitrary perturbations rather than targeted interventions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use size-matched random-feature/direction controls and statistical comparisons to show targeted vectors outperform random.
evidence: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations

confounds.name: SAE sparsity/usage artifacts (high L0 from poor recon or token type)
confounds.detail: High L0 may reflect poor reconstructions or CLS/global-token specialization, not dense mechanisms.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report %ExplainedVar with L0 and analyze token-type utilization; normalize CLS by patch count to contextualize sparsity.
evidence: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video

confounds.name: Probe gains are just better reconstruction
confounds.detail: Higher probe scores might simply follow lower reconstruction error.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Show cases where Equivariant SAEs achieve better probing despite worse reconstruction MSE; analyze inverse correlation.
evidence: Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data

confounds.name: Capacity (overcompleteness) explains SAE advantages
confounds.detail: Improvements could be due to more latents rather than the inductive bias (e.g., equivariance).
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare narrow vs wide baselines to Equivariant SAEs; show gains persist beyond latent-count increases.
evidence: Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data

confounds.name: Verifier incompleteness inflates faithfulness gaps
confounds.detail: Loose certified bounds may exaggerate IRN–model mismatches.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report both verified bounds and attack-derived bounds and their concordant trends across layers.
evidence: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

confounds.name: Underlying model behavior changes under paraphrase
confounds.detail: IRN feature instability could mirror true model changes, not IRN unfaithfulness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure model flip rates under paraphrases and relate to IRN stability metrics per layer.
evidence: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

confounds.name: Constant-feature IRN yields spuriously high stability
confounds.detail: An IRN ignoring the model could appear stable across paraphrases.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Enforce δ-equivalence via formal verification across adversarial sets, ruling out trivial constant-feature solutions.
evidence: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

confounds.name: Collapse due to any equal-size neuron set (not specific)
confounds.detail: Catastrophic failure might follow masking any k neurons, not particular critical ones.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Mask size-matched random neuron sets; compare negligible impact to CAN-selected critical neuron masking.
evidence: Sparse Neuron Ablation Triggers Catastrophic Collapse of the Language Core in Large Vision-Language Models

confounds.name: First-token push suffices to steer generation
confounds.detail: Open-ended steering might be explained by only shifting the first token.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare one-time vs continual injections and per-token logprob changes; show many positions require sustained intervention.
evidence: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations

confounds.name: Sparse single-component sufficiency
confounds.detail: A single head/component might be (mis)attributed as the sole cause of behavior.
confounds.ruled_out_by: One-at-a-time patching vs joint multi-component patching; large joint effects with many small individual effects indicate distributed mechanisms.
evidence: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations

confounds.name: Incorrect module identification / broken hooks
confounds.detail: Misnamed modules or faulty hooks can silently target wrong tensors, invalidating causal claims.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Automated interface validation (shapes, attention-prob normalization, interventions-not-noops, layer-skip causality) before experiments.
evidence: nnterp: A Standardized Interface for Mechanistic Interpretability of Transformers

variants: Token-type configuration controls (CLS-only vs spatial vs all patches)
controls.detail: Train/evaluate SAEs on different token subsets and compare injection/ablation effects.
controls.rules_out: Token-agnostic explanations for SAE effects; attributes differences to token-type specialization.

confounds.name: Ablation-method artifact
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research
confounds.detail: Compact circuits from mean-ablation may not causally reproduce behavior, mimicking positive results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare zero- and mean-ablation against size-matched random circuits; treat mean-ablation circuits cautiously when performance aligns with random.

confounds.name: Redundancy/compensation masks causal roles
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
confounds.detail: Backup components or residual-stream compensation can hide necessity when intervening on a single layer/component.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Patch or ablate multiple hypothesized components jointly; use path patching and multi-layer interventions to reveal masked effects.

confounds.name: Capacity (overcompleteness) explains SAE advantages
evidence: Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data
confounds.detail: Improvements could be due to more latents rather than the inductive bias (e.g., equivariance).
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare narrow vs wide baselines to Equivariant SAEs; show gains persist beyond latent-count increases.

confounds.name: Collapse due to any equal-size neuron set
evidence: Sparse Neuron Ablation Triggers Catastrophic Collapse of the Language Core in Large Vision-Language Models
variants: Collapse due to any equal-size neuron set (not specific)
confounds.detail: Catastrophic failure might follow masking any k neurons, not particular critical ones.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Mask size-matched random neuron sets; compare negligible impact to CAN-selected critical neuron masking.

confounds.name: Constant-feature IRN yields spuriously high stability
evidence: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective
confounds.detail: An IRN ignoring the model could appear stable across paraphrases.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Enforce δ-equivalence via formal verification across adversarial sets, ruling out trivial constant-feature solutions.

confounds.name: Distributed computation/MLP involvement hides true circuit
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research
confounds.detail: Head-only identification may miss layer-level or MLP contributions, yielding false negatives.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Retain entire implicated layers and include MLPs in mappings; compare recovered accuracy with/without MLPs.

confounds.name: First-token push suffices to steer generation
evidence: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations
confounds.detail: Open-ended steering might be explained by only shifting the first token.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare one-time vs continual injections and per-token logprob changes; show many positions require sustained intervention.

confounds.name: General perturbation, not targeted causal change
evidence: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
confounds.detail: Observed corrections could be due to arbitrary perturbations rather than targeted interventions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use size-matched random-feature/direction controls and statistical comparisons to show targeted vectors outperform random.

confounds.name: Incorrect module identification / broken hooks
evidence: nnterp: A Standardized Interface for Mechanistic Interpretability of Transformers
confounds.detail: Misnamed modules or faulty hooks can silently target wrong tensors, invalidating causal claims.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Automated interface validation (shapes, attention-prob normalization, interventions-not-noops, layer-skip causality) before experiments.

confounds.name: Mediation vs amplification/confounding pathways
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
confounds.detail: Component effects may be indirect via other mediators rather than direct interactions.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use path patching to isolate A→B→C vs A→C paths and test necessity/sufficiency per path.

confounds.name: Metric-driven false positives
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
confounds.detail: Improved logit difference can come from suppressing incorrect answers rather than restoring the correct signal.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Inspect individual logits/logprobs and report KL divergence/multiple metrics to detect indiscriminate degradation.

confounds.name: Poor identifiability of SAE features
evidence: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research
confounds.detail: Sparse features may not correspond to causal components, making overlaps incidental.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Quantify SAE–EAP circuit overlap vs random and evaluate recovered accuracy from SAE-selected circuits.

confounds.name: Probe gains are just better reconstruction
evidence: Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data
confounds.detail: Higher probe scores might simply follow lower reconstruction error.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Show cases where Equivariant SAEs achieve better probing despite worse reconstruction MSE; analyze inverse correlation.

confounds.name: Prompt/distribution specificity
evidence: How to use and interpret activation patching
confounds.detail: Effects found on a narrow corruption set may not generalize.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Replicate across multiple corrupted prompt distributions and confirm on a wide distribution varying circuit variables.

experiment_recipes.goal: Establish IOI competence and a clean→corrupt performance gap so patching/ablation effects are meaningful
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Baseline/perturbed runs without patching + Length-matched inputs for content perturbations
metrics: Accuracy / top-k / rank of correct answer
Log probability / probability of target token (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On clean IOI: mean top-1 accuracy >= 0.70 and mean logit difference >= 1.0 nat. On length-matched corrupted IOI: accuracy drops by >= 0.20 absolute vs clean and mean logit difference decreases by >= 1.0 nat vs clean. Failure to meet any gate refutes applicability of subsequent mechanistic tests on this model.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Mechanistic patching requires the model to perform IOI non-trivially and to be sensitive to the corruption; otherwise swaps/ablations have no interpretable effect.

experiment_recipes.goal: Validate intervention/patching instrumentation to ensure swaps are well-formed, causal, and non-noop at alpha>0 and exact no-op at alpha=0
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Instrumentation validation for interventions and hooks
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: All automated hook checks pass (100%): tensor shapes match cached activations; attention prob rows sum to 1.0 within ±1e-5 after intervention; causal layer-skip tests succeed. For a patched run with alpha=0 vs its baseline, mean KL divergence <= 1e-6. For a synthetic non-noop sanity patch (random direction, alpha=1) mean output KL > 1e-6 (not identically zero) and no NaNs/Infs occur. Any failure invalidates subsequent causal claims.
depends_on: Establish IOI competence and a clean→corrupt performance gap so patching/ablation effects are meaningful
experiment_recipes.rationale: Confirms that observed effects arise from intended causal interventions rather than tooling bugs or unintended distribution shifts.

experiment_recipes.goal: Demonstrate standard activation patching norms: denoising/noising symmetry, granularity sweep to components, dose–response, multi-metric agreement, and mediation via path patching
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Activation patching: denoising (clean→corrupt) and noising (corrupt→clean) + Exploratory→confirmatory granularity sweep + Paired-run patching with baseline, perturbed, and patched passes + Intervention-strength (alpha) sweep + Path patching vs component-output patching + Report multiple output metrics per patch
metrics: Log probability / probability of target token (higher_better)
Accuracy / top-k / rank of correct answer (higher_better)
Change in model relevance/logit score after patching (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On corrupted IOI prompts, denoising patch to the identified components (confirmatory granularity) raises mean logit difference by >= 1.0 nat and increases top-1 accuracy to >= 0.80. Reverse noising on clean prompts reduces top-1 accuracy by >= 0.20 absolute and decreases mean logit difference by >= 1.0 nat. Dose–response: for alphas in {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}, Spearman rho between alpha and logit-difference improvement >= 0.8 (p<0.01). Multi-metric agreement: in >= 90% of prompts, sign(logprob_target change) == sign(-KL change); mean KL decreases by >= 5% under denoising vs corrupt baseline. Mediation: path patching achieves >= 50% of the effect size of full component-output patch at confirmatory granularity. Failure of any criterion refutes adherence to standard norms.
depends_on: Validate intervention/patching instrumentation to ensure swaps are well-formed, causal, and non-noop at alpha>0 and exact no-op at alpha=0
experiment_recipes.rationale: Implements core mechanistic interpretability practice: locate causal components via patching, verify necessity/sufficiency with directionality, establish dose–response, cross-metric consistency, and isolate mediated paths.

experiment_recipes.goal: Rule out generic perturbation and ablation-method artifacts via size-matched random controls and zero vs mean ablation baselines
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Size-matched random subset of intervened components/directions + Zero ablation baseline + Mean ablation baseline + Reverse-direction patching (compare denoising vs noising)
metrics: Accuracy / top-k / rank of correct answer (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Targeted denoising patch’s mean logit-difference improvement exceeds the 95th percentile of the size-matched random-control distribution and is >= 2.0× the random-control mean. On clean IOI, zero-ablation of identified components reduces top-1 accuracy by >= 0.20 absolute; mean-ablation reduces accuracy by <= 0.60× the zero-ablation drop (indicating ablation-artifact sensitivity). Reverse-direction check: signs of effects invert between denoising and noising with absolute effect-size ratio in [0.5, 2.0]. Any failure attributes effects to artifacts rather than targeted mechanisms.
depends_on: Demonstrate standard activation patching norms: denoising/noising symmetry, granularity sweep to components, dose–response, multi-metric agreement, and mediation via path patching
experiment_recipes.rationale: Standard practice requires beating random perturbations and diagnosing ablation artifacts; this control attributes effects to specific mechanisms instead of generic damage.

experiment_recipes.goal: Train and validate layerwise Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on model activations with standard reporting of %ExplainedVar and sparsity
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Across non-embedding transformer layers, median %ExplainedVar >= 0.20 and median L0 sparsity <= 64 active features/token; at least 75% of layers meet both criteria. Failure indicates the SAE apparatus is not suitably sparse/faithful for subsequent causal tests.
constraints_not_enforced: Token-type configuration controls (CLS-only vs spatial vs all patches) not applicable to decoder-only LLMs
depends_on: Establish IOI competence and a clean→corrupt performance gap so patching/ablation effects are meaningful
experiment_recipes.rationale: Standard SAE practice reports reconstruction quality and sparsity; thresholds ensure non-degenerate features before causal injections.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test SAE causal faithfulness via reconstruction injection vs ablation with multi-metric reporting
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Layerwise SAE evaluation and injection + Ablation evaluation with zero vs mean ablation + Report multiple output metrics per patch
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Replacing raw activations with SAE reconstructions on clean IOI increases mean cross-entropy by <= 5% and PPL by <= 5% for >= 80% of layers (vs unmodified forward pass), while zero-ablating the same activations increases mean cross-entropy by >= 15% (and KL vs baseline increases correspondingly). Failure indicates SAE features are not sufficiently faithful or causal under standard norms.
depends_on: Train and validate layerwise Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on model activations with standard reporting of %ExplainedVar and sparsity
experiment_recipes.rationale: Mechanistic SAE norms require demonstrating that reconstructions preserve behavior while ablations degrade it, with multiple metrics agreeing.
